c.tagline: Laid-back lakeside capital cradled by Rift Valley hills.

taxi.fareNote: No meters are used; agree on the fare with the driver before departure or book through your hotel.

emergency.medical: No dependable public ambulance system; contact Hôpital Prince Régent Charles or a private clinic directly, or have your hotel arrange transport
emergency.note: Also keep your embassy's emergency line handy; response times can be slow and facilities are limited.

avoid.reason: Avoid the outlying northern quarters such as Kamenge and Kinama and any unlit areas after dark, and check current security advisories as conditions shift.
Petty theft targets phones and bags on the Lake Tanganyika beaches and downtown; move by trusted driver rather than on foot at night.

hood_desc: The leafy diplomatic and government quarter in the city center, with embassies, ministries and tree-lined avenues; a safe, convenient base for business travelers and first-time visitors with solid mid-range hotels.

An elevated hillside enclave above the city offering panoramic views over Lake Tanganyika and the Rift Valley escarpment; quiet, upscale and favored by NGO staff and visitors wanting a peaceful retreat.

An affluent lakeside district south of downtown with tree-lined streets, restaurants and beach clubs on Lake Tanganyika; popular with expats and travelers who want lake access, nightlife and good dining nearby.

The bustling commercial core around the old central market and main boulevards, with banks, budget hotels and abundant street food; convenient and walkable by day but livelier and less secure after dark.
A cooler hillside residential suburb north of downtown, popular with long-stay volunteers and budget travelers for its lower prices, quieter pace and easy access to local markets.

water.note: Tap water is unsafe for visitors; drink bottled or boiled water.

transit.pay: Fares for OTRACO buses and shared minibuses are paid in cash (Burundian francs) directly to the driver or conductor when boarding or alighting; there is no electronic fare card or app-based payment system.
transit.hours: Buses and minibuses generally run from around 6:00 to 19:00; there is little to no organized public transit after dark, so visitors typically use taxis at night.
transit.note: Public buses and minibuses are cheap but crowded and irregular; most visitors and expats rely on private taxis, hotel drivers, or a rented vehicle with driver instead.

bus: Regional coaches to Kigali (Rwanda) and Dar es Salaam (Tanzania)
ferry: Lake Tanganyika passenger/cargo boats to Kigoma, Tanzania (irregular schedule)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% is appreciated at tourist-oriented restaurants and upscale hotels, but not expected elsewhere.
